text:
Drew Doughty's future is the story around him. He's a pending free agent, and the trade-rumor sites have been busy with the Kings' plans for him. He's 36, a two-time Cup winner and a Norris winner, and he has played all 1,293 of his NHL games in Los Angeles.

On the ice, the points have come back after a slow start: six in his last ten games, including a three-assist night in the 6-5 win over Ottawa. But the Kings have only 44% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, eight points worse than without him, and they've scored 5.7 more goals than expected when he's out there. That's a tough combination for a team that's otherwise outchancing opponents.

Last season Evolving-Hockey still had him taking chances away (88th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 14% of entries at his blue line. Our projection sees about 30 points. What the Kings decide matters more than any of these numbers.
